attractions.name: Tanah Lot & Uluwatu temples, Bali
attractions.desc: Tanah Lot sits on a rock formation just offshore, accessible on foot only at low tide, and is one of Bali's most photographed sunset spots. Uluwatu, perched on a clifftop further south, adds dramatic ocean views and an evening Kecak fire dance performance. Both are relatively easy to combine with a day of temple-hopping.

attractions.name: Tegallalang Rice Terraces
attractions.desc: Steep, stepped rice paddies near Ubud built using a centuries-old subak irrigation system still managed communally today. Walking paths wind between the terraces, offering views that shift with the light throughout the day. It's a short drive from Ubud's art markets and yoga studios.

attractions.name: Mount Bromo
attractions.desc: An active volcano in East Java, its smoking crater rising from a vast sea of volcanic sand inside an older, larger caldera. Most visitors arrive before dawn to a nearby viewpoint for sunrise over the surrounding peaks, then descend on foot or horseback to the crater rim. The otherworldly landscape feels far removed from Bali's beaches.

attractions.name: Komodo National Park
attractions.desc: Home to the Komodo dragon, the world's largest living lizard, found in the wild only on a handful of islands in this park. Multi-day boat trips combine dragon-tracking with snorkeling over some of Indonesia's healthiest coral reefs and stops at pink sand beaches. It's a serious undertaking to reach but widely considered worth it.

attractions.name: Borobudur
attractions.desc: The world's largest Buddhist temple, built in the 9th century on the island of Java as a massive stepped pyramid decorated with thousands of relief panels. Climbing to the top, past rows of bell-shaped stupas each containing a Buddha statue, is meant to mirror the path to enlightenment. Sunrise visits are especially popular, with mist often settling over the surrounding volcanoes.

attractions.name: Gili Islands
attractions.desc: Three small, car-free islands off Lombok known for turtle snorkeling, white sand, and a relaxed pace built around bicycles and horse-drawn carts. Gili Trawangan is the liveliest of the three, while Gili Meno and Gili Air stay quieter. They're a common add-on after Bali for travelers wanting fewer crowds.

itinerary.label: Days 1–4
itinerary.title: Bali
itinerary.desc: Ubud's rice terraces, Tanah Lot and Uluwatu temples, and the Gili Islands as a side trip.
itinerary.cost: Ubud's rice terrace entry fees run IDR 15,000–25,000; a day trip to the Gili Islands by fast boat costs about $40–60 round trip.
itinerary.food: Try babi guling (Balinese roast suckling pig), best from a local warung rather than a tourist restaurant.

itinerary.label: Days 5–6
itinerary.title: Mount Bromo
itinerary.desc: Fly to Java for a sunrise volcano trek and crater visit.
itinerary.logistics: ~1h flight to Surabaya, then a drive
itinerary.cost: Park entry plus jeep tour for the sunrise trek runs about $30–50 per person.
itinerary.food: Grab a hot bowl of bakso (meatball soup) at the base before the early sunrise trek — it's cold up there.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.title: Borobudur & Yogyakarta
itinerary.desc: The great Buddhist temple and the nearby royal city.
itinerary.logistics: ~5h drive from Bromo, or fly via Surabaya
itinerary.cost: Borobudur entry costs about $25 for foreigners (sunrise tickets cost more).
itinerary.food: Try gudeg, Yogyakarta's signature sweet jackfruit stew, a genuine regional specialty.

itinerary.label: Days 8–11
itinerary.title: Komodo National Park
itinerary.desc: A multi-day boat trip combining dragon-tracking with snorkeling and beach stops.
itinerary.logistics: ~1h flight from Yogyakarta to Labuan Bajo
itinerary.cost: Multi-day boat tours with dragon-tracking and snorkeling run $150–300+ depending on the boat class.
itinerary.food: Fresh-grilled fish on the boat, caught the same day, is a highlight of most Komodo tours.

goodToKnow.tipping: Not obligatory; rounding up or 10% at nicer restaurants is appreciated
goodToKnow.safety: Generally safe; take normal precautions with rental scooters and ocean currents
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Domestic flights are essential for island-hopping given the country's size
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Bali's Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS) is the main gateway for this route; Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta (CGK) is Indonesia's largest hub if arriving via the capital first

food.name: Nasi goreng
food.desc: Indonesia's beloved fried rice, typically topped with a fried egg and crispy shallots.

food.name: Satay
food.desc: Grilled skewered meat served with a rich peanut sauce.

food.name: Rendang
food.desc: A slow-cooked beef dish simmered in coconut milk and spices until deeply tender.

food.name: Gado-gado
food.desc: A vegetable salad with hard-boiled egg, tofu, and peanut sauce dressing.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Bali?
faq.a: Most Western passport holders get a Visa on Arrival (30 days, extendable once for another 30, about $35/IDR 500,000) or can apply for the same online in advance as an e-VOA.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Bali's Ngurah Rai (DPS) for this route; Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta (CGK) if arriving via the capital first.

faq.q: Is there a Bali tourist tax?
faq.a: Yes, a one-time IDR 150,000 (about $10) tourist levy applies specifically to Bali, payable online before arrival or at the airport.

faq.q: Is tap water safe to drink in Indonesia?
faq.a: No — stick to bottled or filtered water throughout, including for brushing teeth.

daysReason: 11 days covers Bali, Mount Bromo, Borobudur, and Komodo National Park without rushing. 4–5 works for just Bali; 14+ lets you slow down or add Lombok.
visa: Visa on arrival is available for most nationalities for short stays — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Templos de Tanah Lot e Uluwatu
attractions.desc: Tanah Lot situa-se numa formação rochosa ao largo, acessível a pé apenas na maré baixa, e é um dos pontos de pôr do sol mais fotografados de Bali. Uluwatu, empoleirado num penhasco mais a sul, acrescenta vistas dramáticas sobre o oceano e uma performance noturna de dança de fogo Kecak. Ambos são relativamente fáceis de combinar com um dia a visitar templos.

attractions.name: Socalcos de Arroz de Tegallalang
attractions.desc: Arrozais íngremes e em socalcos perto de Ubud, construídos usando um sistema de irrigação subak centenário ainda gerido comunitariamente hoje. Caminhos serpenteiam entre os socalcos, oferecendo vistas que mudam com a luz ao longo do dia. Fica a uma curta distância de carro dos mercados de arte e estúdios de yoga de Ubud.

attractions.name: Monte Bromo
attractions.desc: Um vulcão ativo em Java Oriental, com a sua cratera fumegante a erguer-se de um vasto mar de areia vulcânica dentro de uma caldeira maior e mais antiga. A maioria dos visitantes chega antes do amanhecer a um miradouro próximo para ver o nascer do sol sobre os picos circundantes, depois desce a pé ou a cavalo até à borda da cratera. A paisagem de outro mundo sente-se muito distante das praias de Bali.

attractions.name: Parque Nacional de Komodo
attractions.desc: Casa do dragão de Komodo, o maior lagarto vivo do mundo, encontrado na natureza apenas numa mão-cheia de ilhas dentro deste parque. Viagens de barco de vários dias combinam o rastreio de dragões com mergulho com snorkel sobre alguns dos recifes de coral mais saudáveis da Indonésia e paragens em praias de areia rosa. É um empreendimento sério de alcançar mas amplamente considerado que vale a pena.

attractions.name: Borobudur
attractions.desc: O maior templo budista do mundo, construído no século IX na ilha de Java como uma pirâmide escalonada maciça decorada com milhares de painéis de relevo. Subir até ao topo, passando por fileiras de stupas em forma de sino contendo cada uma uma estátua de Buda, pretende espelhar o caminho para a iluminação. Visitas ao amanhecer são especialmente populares, muitas vezes com neblina a assentar sobre os vulcões circundantes.

attractions.name: Ilhas Gili
attractions.desc: Três pequenas ilhas sem carros ao largo de Lombok, conhecidas pelo mergulho com tartarugas, areia branca, e um ritmo relaxado construído à volta de bicicletas e carroças puxadas a cavalo. Gili Trawangan é a mais animada das três, enquanto Gili Meno e Gili Air permanecem mais tranquilas. São um acrescento comum depois de Bali para viajantes que querem menos multidões.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–4
itinerary.title: Bali
itinerary.desc: Os socalcos de arroz de Ubud, os templos de Tanah Lot e Uluwatu, e as Ilhas Gili como excursão.

itinerary.label: Dias 5–6
itinerary.title: Monte Bromo
itinerary.desc: Voa até Java para um trekking ao vulcão ao amanhecer e visita à cratera.
itinerary.logistics: ~1h de voo até Surabaya, depois uma condução

itinerary.label: Dia 7
itinerary.title: Borobudur e Yogyakarta
itinerary.desc: O grande templo budista e a cidade real próxima.
itinerary.logistics: ~5h de carro desde Bromo, ou voo via Surabaya

itinerary.label: Dias 8–11
itinerary.title: Parque Nacional de Komodo
itinerary.desc: Uma viagem de barco de vários dias que combina rastreio de dragões com mergulho e paragens de praia.
itinerary.logistics: ~1h de voo desde Yogyakarta até Labuan Bajo

goodToKnow.tipping: Não é obrigatório; arredondar para cima ou 10% em restaurantes melhores é apreciado
goodToKnow.safety: Geralmente seguro; precauções normais com scooters alugadas e correntes oceânicas
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Voos domésticos são essenciais para saltar entre ilhas dado o tamanho do país
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Bali's Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS) is the main gateway for this route; Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta (CGK) is Indonesia's largest hub if arriving via the capital first

food.name: Rendang
